meta.assignment: Recommend two minimal, openly usable NeuroML v2 fixture models for the NeuroSem pilot
meta.procedure_order: For every repository whose files were downloaded, repository metadata and the LICENSE text were read via the GitHub REST API first; model files were fetched only afterwards, from raw.githubusercontent.com URLs pinned to a commit SHA, into the scratch folder (never into the NeuroSem repo).

local_tooling_used.note: Versions below are what pip resolved in the scratch venv on 2026-09-13 and match the PyPI JSON API responses retrieved the same day.
local_tooling_used.java: not installed; jnml / jNeuroML not run locally

meta.validation_method_note: Pure-Python structural check = neuroml.utils.validate_neuroml2 from libNeuroML 0.6.7 (source inspected in venv: loads the file with include_includes=True and runs recursive validation; bundled schemas NeuroML_v2beta1..v2beta5, v2.0..v2.3.1). pyneuroml.pynml.validate_neuroml2 was also inspected: it shells out to jnml (Java), so it was not usable here. jnml -validate evidence therefore comes only from the repositories' own GitHub Actions OMV logs.
important_caveats: No held-out evaluation was created or accessed.

No NeuroSem results are claimed. Behaviour descriptions come from the repositories' own OMV expected-spike-time files (.mep) plus simple arithmetic on those numbers. Where a mechanism is named (for example adaptation or rebound), it is an expectation to confirm by simulation in M1, not a verified result.
Passing OMV/CI tests is finite testing and is not proof of equivalence or correctness.
Local runtime under jNeuroML is unmeasured because Java is absent.

recommended_pair: Pospischil2008_RS: OpenSourceBrain/PospischilEtAl2008 @ 049081c39357d9e7c478b63ef7b10f374d1c50f4, NeuroML2/cells/RS (single-compartment regular-spiking cell with M-current; the reference spike train shows lengthening interspike intervals)

Pospischil2008_LTS: OpenSourceBrain/PospischilEtAl2008 @ 049081c39357d9e7c478b63ef7b10f374d1c50f4, NeuroML2/cells/LTS (single-compartment low-threshold-spiking cell with T-type Ca current and a Ca pool; suited to hyperpolarisation and rebound protocols)
backups: Pospischil2008_FS (same repo/SHA; tonic non-adapting spiking; strict libNeuroML-valid)
NeuroML2_SingleCompHHCell / LEMS_NML2_Ex5_DetCell (NeuroML/NeuroML2 @ a5f5dad; LGPL-3.0; canonical HH 1952 teaching model)
WangBuzsaki1996 wb1 cell (OpenSourceBrain/WangBuzsaki1996 @ c532284; MIT for NeuroML2 dir; fast tonic interneuron)
Pospischil2008_IB (same repo/SHA; high-threshold Ca IL + IM; labelled intrinsically bursting)
rationale: The recommended pair is RS and LTS from the OpenSourceBrain conversion of Pospischil et al. 2008. Both cells come from one peer-reviewed paper with a Crossref-verified DOI and a ModelDB entry. The repository's LICENSE applies MIT to everything outside the NEURON_ORIG and NEURON_MODIFIED folders, and all NeuroML2 files sit outside those folders. Both cells are true single-compartment, conductance-based models (one soma segment each; confirmed by loading them with libNeuroML). Both have OMV tests that ran in GitHub Actions at the pinned commit (run 30447139603, 2026-07-29): the jNeuroML, jNeuroML_validate, jNeuroML_NEURON, NEURON and NetPyNE jobs succeeded, and only the jNeuroML_Moose job on Python 3.10 failed. The two cells behave differently, which the pilot protocols need. RS has the slow M-type K current, and its reference spike train shows interspike intervals lengthening from 28 to 135 ms. LTS adds a T-type Ca current and a Ca pool, and its reference shows an early spike pair aligned with Ca transients, so hyperpolarising-step and release-rebound protocols should be informative. The main caveat, which Neel must decide on, is that LTS's IT channel uses custom LEMS ComponentTypes. libNeuroML 0.6.7's strict XSD validation rejects IT.channel.nml, LTS.cell.nml and LTS.net.nml, while jnml -validate passed on LTS.net.nml and LTS.cell.nml in CI. NeuroSem therefore has to name jnml -validate as its structural-validity oracle, which fits the handoff's 'jNeuroML only' pilot. If Neel wants both fixtures to pass strict pure-Python validation, replace LTS with the NeuroML2 SingleCompHHCell/Ex5 example: it is LGPL-3.0, from an independent source, and passed strict validation plus jNeuroML and PyLEMS OMV checks. That swap loses the rebound/T-current behaviour. Both recommended cells share channel files from one repository, so they are correlated. That is acceptable for a two-model pilot but not as independent evidence for held-out-model generalisation. Allen Cell Types models were excluded: their NeuroML2 biophysical cells are large morphology files, the GLIF conversions are integrate-and-fire, and the Allen-derived content falls under Allen Institute terms of use with no named open license. The ModelDB mirror repositories for Ih and T-current models were excluded because they have no LICENSE and no NeuroML files.

candidates.license_detail: The GitHub API reports spdx NOASSERTION because LICENSE opens with a custom preamble. The full MIT text follows (Copyright 2018 Open Source Brain developers) and applies to all software except the NEURON_ORIG and NEURON_MODIFIED directories. Code in those two directories is provided on condition of citing the ModelDB entry and the original publication (CITATION.md). The NeuroML2/ files are therefore MIT. The .mep reference files under NEURON_MODIFIED carry the citation condition.

candidates.expected_behavior: Expected spike times from the OMV reference (NEURON_MODIFIED/.test.RS.spikes.mep, generated with the modified NEURON scripts): 320.554, 348.522, 387.944, 456.69, 592.105 ms. The interspike intervals are about 28.0, 39.4, 68.7 and 135.4 ms and lengthen progressively, a pattern consistent with spike-frequency adaptation. Adaptation mediated by IM is the expected mechanism but is not verified here; NeuroSem M1/M2 simulation must confirm it. OMV compares jNeuroML output with these times at relative tolerance 0.00218373430388.
candidates.validation_evidence: (1) libNeuroML 0.6.7 strict validation: VALID for RS.cell.nml, RS.net.nml, Na/Kd/IM/Leak channel files. (2) GitHub Actions 'Continuous build using OMV' run 30447139603 (2026-07-29) at the pinned SHA: jobs jNeuroML (py3.10, py3.12), jNeuroML_validate, jNeuroML_NEURON, NEURON, jNeuroML_NetPyNE and jNeuroML_Moose:4.0.0.dev20240411 succeeded; only 'build (3.10, jNeuroML_Moose)' failed, at its OMV step. The same pattern appears in run 26042274142 (2026-05-18). Runs 19683390438 and 19683226292 at the same SHA (2025-11-25) were fully successful. (3) The py3.12 jNeuroML job log shows the NeuroML2/cells/RS/.test.RS.spikes.LEMS.omt spike-times check passed. (4) OMV engine files in the repo also cover MOOSE, NetPyNE and NEURON for RS.
candidates.runtime_notes: Not measured locally (no Java). The reference LEMS run is 1000 ms at dt 0.001 ms, which is 1e6 steps, so the cost of a multi-protocol battery under jNeuroML must be measured in M1. The repo's NeuroML2/cells/summary folder contains Sweep.py, GenerateExamples.py and dt-comparison figures (dt_traces_RS.png, heatmap_dt_RS.png), which suggests a timestep-sensitivity sweep was done upstream; its contents were not inspected. Execution should be deterministic: the only input is a pulseGenerator, and no noise or random components were found in the inspected files. Run-to-run determinism was not tested locally for this model.
candidates.protocol_suitability: Good for zero-current baseline, weak depolarising step, rheobase search, a fixed multiple of rheobase, a long suprathreshold step (ISI, adaptation-index features), a depolarising ramp, and short pulses and paired pulses. The hyperpolarising step should give a mainly passive deflection; the cell has no Ih, so no sag is expected, and hyperpolarisation-release rebound is likely uninformative. That is an expectation, not a result.
candidates.concerns: License detection returns NOASSERTION, so record the exact LICENSE text and its directory exceptions. The latest archived release (Zenodo v0.1, 2018) predates the pinned commit, so the fixture pin is a commit SHA, not a release DOI. schemaLocation references an old beta schema, although validation passes. The Moose CI job is currently failing (not needed for a jNeuroML-only pilot). The .mep reference spike times come from the NEURON_MODIFIED scripts, which carry a citation condition. RS shares channel files with LTS/FS/IB, so these fixtures are correlated and cannot serve as independent held-out models. The OSB conversion used modified NEURON scripts (NEURON_MODIFIED/diffs_to_original.txt lists changes such as FARADAY constants and the solver METHOD), so the NeuroML model is matched to the modified scripts, not bit-identical to the original ModelDB code.

candidates.model_name: Pospischil2008_LTS (low-threshold-spiking cell with T-type Ca current, NeuroML2 conversion)
candidates.license_detail: Same repository LICENSE as rank 1: MIT for NeuroML2/, with a citation condition on NEURON_ORIG and NEURON_MODIFIED (the .mep reference file lives in the latter).
candidates.original_citation: Pospischil M, Toledo-Rodriguez M, Monier C, Piwkowska Z, Bal T, Fregnac Y, Markram H, Destexhe A. Minimal Hodgkin-Huxley type models for different classes of cortical and thalamic neurons. Biological Cybernetics 99(4-5):427-441, 2008. doi:10.1007/s00422-008-0263-8. ModelDB 123623. The IT channel file's notes say its kinetics are based on data from Huguenard & McCormick 1992 and Huguenard & Prince 1992; that attribution is as stated in the file and was not independently verified.
candidates.neuroml_version_or_schema: Files declare NeuroML_v2beta4.xsd. libNeuroML 0.6.7 strict validation FAILS for IT.channel.nml, LTS.cell.nml and LTS.net.nml with the same error: gate 's' has type 'IT_s_gate' (line 52 of IT.channel.nml), which is not in the XSD gateTypes enumeration. IT_s_gate is a custom LEMS ComponentType defined in the same file, extending gateHHtauInf; IT_s_inf_inf, IT_u_tau_tau and IT_u_inf_inf are also custom. By contrast, jnml -validate on LTS.net.nml and LTS.cell.nml completed successfully in CI run 30447139603 (NeuroML2/cells/LTS/.test.validate.omt). NeuroML2/channels/IT has no .test.validate.omt, so IT.channel.nml was not validated standalone in CI. Whether jnml -validate descends into included files is unverified. Ca.nml and the other channel files passed libNeuroML validation.
candidates.single_compartment: yes: one segment 'Soma' (diameter 96.0 um), libNeuroML loader reports segments=1
candidates.channels: LeakConductance 1e-5 S/cm2 (erev -85 mV); Na 0.05 S/cm2 (erev 50 mV); Kd 0.005 S/cm2 (erev -100 mV); IM 3e-5 S/cm2 (erev -100 mV); IT low-threshold (T-type) Ca, channelDensityNernst 4e-4 S/cm2, gates s^2 (instantaneous activation, custom ComponentType) and u (tau/inf custom ComponentTypes, q10ExpTemp q10Factor 3 at 24 degC); intracellular Ca species with CaPoolModel (Ca.nml), initial [Ca]in 2.4e-4 mM, [Ca]out 2.0 mM. Cm 1.0 uF/cm2, initMembPotential -84 mV, network temperature 36 degC.
candidates.reference_protocol_in_repo: pulseGenerator 0.15 nA (1.5E-10 A), delay 400 ms, duration 400 ms; LEMS simulation 1000 ms, step 0.001 ms; outputs LTS.dat (v), LTS.cai.dat ([Ca]), LTS.eca.dat (Ca reversal)
candidates.expected_behavior: OMV reference (NEURON_MODIFIED/.test.LTS.spikes.mep): voltage spike times 431.423, 445.189, 517.237, 720.422 ms, and [Ca] threshold crossings (0.0009 mM) at 430.315 and 443.502 ms. The first two spikes, 13.8 ms apart, coincide with Ca transients and are followed by sparse later spikes. That fits an initial low-threshold Ca-driven response, but the interpretation is unverified. The cell includes IT, so a post-inhibitory rebound response after release from hyperpolarisation is the scientific reason to pick it. No repository test exercises hyperpolarisation or rebound, so rebound behaviour is unverified and must be checked by simulation in M1/M3.
candidates.validation_evidence: (1) CI run 30447139603 at the pinned SHA: the py3.12 jNeuroML job log shows NeuroML2/cells/LTS/.test.LTS.spikes.LEMS.omt passed both observables (voltage spike times and [Ca] 'ca spikes'), and NeuroML2/channels/IT/.test.IT.nonernst.LEMS.omt passed; the py3.12 jNeuroML_validate job log shows jnml -validate LTS.net.nml LTS.cell.nml completed successfully. The jNeuroML_NEURON and NEURON jobs in that run also succeeded. (2) libNeuroML 0.6.7 strict validation: INVALID (see neuroml_version_or_schema). (3) Only the jNeuroML_Moose py3.10 job failed in that run.
candidates.runtime_notes: Not measured locally (no Java). The reference run is 1000 ms at dt 0.001 ms (1e6 steps). The model carries extra state (Ca pool, Nernst reversal), and the IT gate uses an instantaneous (tau=0) activation, which may make it stiffer or more dt-sensitive; this needs checking in the h, h/2, h/4 tolerance calibration. Execution should be deterministic: the only input is a pulseGenerator, and no stochastic elements were found in the inspected files.
candidates.protocol_suitability: Best candidate among those inspected for hyperpolarising-step and hyperpolarisation-release rebound protocols (T-type current present) and for first-spike latency and burst-count features. Also usable for depolarising steps and rheobase. No Ih, so a sag ratio is not expected to be meaningful.
candidates.concerns: BLOCKER-LEVEL DECISION: validators disagree (libNeuroML strict XSD rejects the file; jnml -validate accepts it in CI). NeuroSem must fix jnml -validate, with its version recorded, as the structural-validity oracle; otherwise every LTS mutant would be classed 'structurally invalid' by the pure-Python checker. The custom LEMS ComponentTypes put kinetic expressions in LEMS strings, so mutation operators and valid transformations (unit conversion, renaming) must handle LEMS-level expressions and references, not just NeuroML attributes. The IT file's annotation labels the channel as 'K channels', an upstream metadata inconsistency (observed at line 43); the file is ISO-8859-1 encoded. Rebound behaviour is unverified. The cell shares channel files and provenance with RS, so the pair is correlated. Same Zenodo-release versus commit-pin and NEURON_MODIFIED citation-condition notes as rank 1.

candidates.protocol_suitability: Good for baseline, weak step, rheobase, fixed-multiple step, ramp, short and paired pulses. Adaptation, sag and T-type rebound features are not expected to be informative. The example is fast enough to serve as a smoke-test fixture for pipeline plumbing.
candidates.concerns: LGPL-3.0 is weak copyleft: redistributing modified mutant files may carry LGPL obligations, and compatibility with NeuroSem's chosen license is a decision for Neel. The file lives in the language-specification repository, where examples can change between commits (pin the SHA). It is a textbook implementation rather than a paper-specific curated model. LEMS_NML2_Ex5_DetCell.xml includes the NML file by relative path (../examples/) and writes to results/, so fixture layout must preserve relative paths. Behaviour is similar to FS/WB (tonic), so it adds little firing-regime diversity.

candidates.protocol_suitability: Potentially useful later for burst-count and adaptation features; long-step protocols needed. Weaker than LTS for rebound.
candidates.concerns: The reference stimulus is truncated by the simulation length. Its firing-regime interpretation is unverified. It shares provenance and channel files with RS/LTS/FS. The IL channel has a fixed Ca reversal (not Nernst), unlike IT in LTS.

excluded_or_not_selected.item: OpenSourceBrain/AllenInstituteNeuroML (Allen Cell Types models converted to NeuroML2)
excluded_or_not_selected.finding: The repo LICENSE applies MIT to OSB software but carves out content reused from the Allen Cell Types Database (copyright 2015 Allen Institute). The Allen Institute terms of use restrict redistribution for commercial purposes, require attribution per their citation policy, and name no open license. The NeuroML2 biophysical cell files (Cell_*.cell.nml) are 0.4 to 1.4 MB each per the Git tree sizes, consistent with detailed morphologies, so they are not minimal single-compartment fixtures; not downloaded. The GLIF conversions are generalized leaky integrate-and-fire variants per models/GLIF/README.md, not conductance-based HH-type models. CI at bd54a29 succeeded. Excluded for the pilot; license terms would need separate review before any use.

The about page (fetched with curl) states only an image-use policy (images CC Attribution); no model-level license statement was found, so each model's license must be traced to its original source. The search page is JavaScript-rendered (485-byte HTML via curl, no model IDs extractable); WebFetch failed with a certificate-chain error. No individual NeuroML-DB model records were evaluated; this remains unverified. Database paper verified via Crossref: Birgiolas J, Haynes V, Gleeson P, Gerkin RC, Dietrich SW, Crook S. NeuroML-DB: Sharing and characterizing data-driven neuroscience models described in NeuroML. PLOS Computational Biology 19(3):e1010941, 2023. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010941.

License BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE.txt, GitHub API). Not selected because the handoff prefers conductance-based models, and the repo description points to the Izhikevich simple-model publication page; files not inspected.

GitHub code search (hcn, extension:nml, org:OpenSourceBrain) returned 103 hits, dominated by multi-compartment Blue Brain and Allen cells plus channel files in OpenCortex (examples/Balanced/Ih.channel.nml) and NetPyNEShowcase (NeuroML2/chanDens/HCN.channel.nml). No clearly licensed, minimal single-compartment cell with Ih was identified in the time available; this remains an open gap for a later sag-ratio fixture.
LICENSE present (GitHub spdx NOASSERTION); model files not inspected, and no single-compartment status was established. Not evaluated further.
